---
title: "storecard"
subtitle: "Store cards and assertions for array stores"
---

A **store card** is a small, metadata-only description of an array store:
what its grid is, how it is chunked and compressed, where its bytes live, and
whether a given reader can use it. A card is built from a URL by reading a
few kilobytes of metadata, never a data chunk.

Where a store hides a simple grid behind coordinate arrays, or gets a fill
value or a CRS wrong, the fix is an **assertion**: a separate, evidenced,
versioned claim about someone else's store, which supplies what it lacks
without copying or editing a byte of it.

## See it work

[Five costumes, one grid](demo/costumes.html): five published Zarr stores
hold the same sea ice on the same polar stereographic grid, each declaring it
differently: CF with 1-D axes, CF with a renamed grid mapping, a transform
with an EPSG code and a pyramid, a transform with PROJJSON only, and nothing
but 2-D longitude and latitude. Four common reader rules each place a
different subset. The card reads every declaration, checks they agree, and
places the first four, which then draw identically cell for cell.

[One assertion, end to end](demo/index.html): two published Zarr stores hold
the same Antarctic sea ice. One declares its grid in six numbers and a CRS;
the other hides the same grid behind 68 MB of 2-D longitude and latitude, so
a reader that wants a declared grid refuses it. The page applies a published
assertion of 2 KB to the second store, in the browser, and checks that it
then draws identically to the first: every value, the transform, the CRS and
every pixel.

## The idea in three lines

- **Cards are facts, not opinions.** A spec's conformance, a viewer's
  capabilities and house rules are thresholds over cards, so any number of
  them can be checked against one card. See [The card](card.qmd).
- **Assertions, not edits.** A fix is a document keyed to the store's URL and
  a digest of its metadata, with its evidence and who made it. It can be
  emitted as zarr-conventions attributes, a STAC patch or a GDAL VRT. See
  [Assertions](assertions.qmd).
- **Inference is narrow and checked.** `storecard.fit` tests a card's
  coordinate sample against a short list of published frames and either
  asserts one or refuses with the residual of every frame tried. Open-ended
  inference belongs to [degredation](ecosystem.qmd). See [Grid fit](fit.qmd).

## Try it

```sh
pip install -e .                      # zarr and numpy; add [remote] for s3:// and https://
storecard path/to/store.zarr          # or: python -m storecard URL --stac collection.json
python -m storecard URL --stac COLLECTION --fit
storecard URL --assertion assertions/f03d-asi-latlon2d.json --emit vrt
```

## Where it stands

| Step | State |
| ---- | ----- |
| 1. Card extractor, URL in, card out | Zarr v2 and v3 done, checked against every published fixture. Icechunk, kerchunk and CORS probing of referenced-chunk hosts to do |
| 2. Grid fit from a card | Named frames done: f03d recovers EPSG:3412 exactly, the tripolar f08c is refused |
| 3. One assertion end to end | Done: [the demo](demo/index.html). The same overlay in portolan-browser is open |
| 4. Cards over the `ausantarctic` stores on source.coop | Next |
| 5. Rule packs and viewer capability matching | Later |

The project brief, with decisions and open questions, is
[BRIEF.md](https://github.com/hypertidy/storecard/blob/main/BRIEF.md).
